title: Expressions
subtitle: Write, Read, Evaluate
bounds: No negatives anywhere. Prompt constants: added numbers 1-20, multipliers and divisors 2-10. T3 (evaluate): a substituted value is 2-10 where it is multiplied or squared and 1-20 where it is only added or subtracted; every x step a times-table fact (both values <= 10), powers are squares of 2-10 or cubes of 2-4, every step and the answer whole and 0-100. T4/T5: every coefficient product a times-table fact, every combined coefficient and constant 1-100, like-term sums of numbers <= 20.

tiers.name: Words to Expressions
tiers.description: Turn words into an expression: 5 less than n is n − 5.

tiers.name: Parts of an Expression
tiers.description: Terms, coefficients, constants, and naming an expression by its last step.

tiers.name: Evaluate
tiers.description: Put the number in for the letter, then follow the order of operations.

tiers.name: Distributive Property
tiers.description: Expand a(b + c) and factor out the greatest common factor.

tiers.name: Equivalent Expressions
tiers.description: Combine like terms and spot expressions that are always equal.

ORDER_SUB.student: Order matters for −. '5 less than n' starts at n: n − 5.
ORDER_SUB.teacher: Writes subtraction in the order the words appear: '5 less than n' as 5 − n.

SWAP_DIV.student: Order matters for ÷. 'n divided by 3' starts with n: n ÷ 3.
SWAP_DIV.teacher: Reverses dividend and divisor when translating a quotient.

WRONG_OP.student: Match the words: sum +, difference −, product ×, quotient ÷.
WRONG_OP.teacher: Translates an operation word into the wrong operation.

MISSING_PARENS.student: 'Times the sum' multiplies the WHOLE sum, so use ( ): 3(n + 4).
MISSING_PARENS.teacher: Omits grouping symbols: '3 times the sum of n and 4' as 3n + 4.

EXTRA_PARENS.student: '3 more than 2n' adds 3 after multiplying: 2n + 3, no ( ).
EXTRA_PARENS.teacher: Adds grouping that the phrase does not have: '3 more than 2n' as 2(n + 3).

SWAPPED_NUMS.student: Check which number multiplies and which number is added or taken away.
SWAPPED_NUMS.teacher: Puts each constant in the other's role (multiplier vs addend).

COEF_CONST_MIX.student: Coefficient: the number times a letter. Constant: a number all alone.
COEF_CONST_MIX.teacher: Confuses the coefficient with the constant term.

TERM_FOR_COEF.student: That's the whole term. The coefficient is just its number: 7 in 7x.
TERM_FOR_COEF.teacher: Gives the whole term when asked for its coefficient.

VARIABLE_FOR_NUMBER.student: That's the letter (the variable). The question asks for a number.
VARIABLE_FOR_NUMBER.teacher: Gives the variable when asked for a coefficient or constant.

HIDDEN_ONE.student: A letter alone has coefficient 1: y means 1y.
HIDDEN_ONE.teacher: Says a bare variable has coefficient 0 (or none).

OTHER_VARIABLE.student: That number goes with a different letter. Find the one in front of it.
OTHER_VARIABLE.teacher: Gives the coefficient of a different variable.

VARIABLE_TERM.student: A constant has no letter. In 4a + 9 the constant is 9.
VARIABLE_TERM.teacher: Names a variable term (or the variable) as the constant term.

COUNTS_VARIABLES.student: A number alone is a term too: 3a + 2b + 5 has 3 terms.
COUNTS_VARIABLES.teacher: Counts only the terms that contain a variable.

COUNTS_PIECES.student: A term is a whole piece between + signs: 3a is one term, not two.
COUNTS_PIECES.teacher: Counts every number and letter separately instead of terms.

INNER_OP.student: Name it by the LAST step: 2(x + 5) adds first, multiplies last: product.
INNER_OP.teacher: Names an expression by an inner operation rather than the last one done.

LAST_STEP.student: Find the step you'd do last. That step names it: sum, product...
LAST_STEP.teacher: Names an expression by an operation it does not use last (or at all).

CONCAT.student: 3x means 3 times x. With x = 5 it is 3 × 5 = 15, not 35.
CONCAT.teacher: Substitutes by writing digits side by side: 3x with x = 5 read as 35.

ADD_COEF.student: A number next to a letter means multiply: 3x is 3 × x, not 3 + x.
ADD_COEF.teacher: Adds the coefficient to the value instead of multiplying.

ORDER.student: Multiply before you add, unless ( ) say otherwise.
ORDER.teacher: Evaluates left to right or adds before multiplying, ignoring precedence.

EXP_AS_TIMES.student: x^2 means x × x, not x × 2. So 4^2 = 16.
EXP_AS_TIMES.teacher: Reads an exponent as a multiplier: x^2 as 2x.

SQUARE_PRODUCT.student: In 2a^2 only a is squared: square a first, then times 2.
SQUARE_PRODUCT.teacher: Squares the coefficient too: 2a^2 evaluated as (2a)^2.

PARENS_SKIPPED.student: Work inside ( ) first: 5(x − 2) is 5 times the whole (x − 2).

PARTIAL_DIST.teacher: Distributes to the first term only.

ADD_FOR_MUL.student: The outside number multiplies each term: 3(x + 4) = 3x + 12.
ADD_FOR_MUL.teacher: Adds the outside factor to a term instead of multiplying it.

SIGN_DROP.teacher: Loses a subtraction sign when distributing or combining.

UNLIKE_COMBINED.student: Only like terms combine. 3x + 12 can't become 15x.
UNLIKE_COMBINED.teacher: Combines unlike terms (a variable term with a constant).

PARTIAL_FACTOR.student: Divide EVERY term by the factor you take out: 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3).
PARTIAL_FACTOR.teacher: Factors the GCF out of one term only.

SUB_FOR_DIV.teacher: Subtracts the common factor from each term instead of dividing.

X_FROM_BOTH.student: Only take out what EVERY term has. 9 has no x, so x can't come out.
X_FROM_BOTH.teacher: Factors a variable out of a term that does not contain it.

POWER_FOR_SUM.student: Adding like terms adds the numbers: x + x + x = 3x, not x^3.
POWER_FOR_SUM.teacher: Turns repeated addition into a power (x + x = x^2).

SUM_FOR_POWER.student: y × y is y^2. Adding gives 2y; multiplying gives y^2.
SUM_FOR_POWER.teacher: Turns repeated multiplication into a coefficient (y × y = 2y).

MULT_COEF.student: Add like terms: 5a + 3a is 8a. Multiply only when you see ×.
MULT_COEF.teacher: Multiplies the coefficients when combining like terms.

DROPPED_TERM.student: Keep every term. Count all the x terms before you stop.
DROPPED_TERM.teacher: Leaves a like term uncombined or drops it.
